questions.question: Explain two causes of poverty in Elizabethan England. (4 marks)
questions.correctAnswer: Two causes: (1) Enclosure - landowners fenced off common land for sheep farming, depriving peasants of the land they needed for grazing and growing food, driving them off the land into towns; (2) Rising population - the population grew from 2.5 million to over 4 million between 1500 and 1600, creating more demand for food, housing, and jobs than the economy could supply. questions.question: What was the difference between the "deserving poor" and the "undeserving poor"? (4 marks)
questions.correctAnswer: The "deserving poor" were those who were poor through no fault of their own - the old, sick, disabled, widows, and orphans - and were considered worthy of sympathy and help. The "undeserving poor" were the able-bodied who could work but chose not to - vagrants, beggars, and the idle - who were considered morally responsible for their poverty and deserving of punishment rather than help.

questions.question: Describe the punishments that could be given to vagrants under the 1572 Vagabond Act. (4 marks)
questions.correctAnswer: Under the 1572 Act: first offence - public whipping and burning through the right ear with a hot iron; second offence - imprisonment or deportation; third offence - execution as a felon. Vagrants were also to be returned to their home parish. The punishments were deliberately harsh and public to deter others.
